verdicts.reason: audio_play_story_file writes (and then printf-reads) *out_resume_offset on a barge-in with no null guard. Two live callers pass story_barge_in_poll with out_resume_offset == nullptr, so any press during the greeting or the bedtime music dereferences address 0 (StoreProhibited, panic, reboot). The greeting is the first thing every first menu of a boot plays, and the code comment says an impatient child pressing during the hello is intended to be allowed. The finding's fix list misses a second deref: the Serial.printf right after the write also reads *out_resume_offset (audio_io.cpp:436 and :645), so guarding only the assignment still crashes (LoadProhibited).

Stream variant :430/:436 has the same pattern but both of its callers (:1817, :2405) pass a real pointer. Secondary also confirmed: only :527 sets s_browse_request and only browse_take_request() (:1945, inside the same session) clears it, so once the null write is guarded, a GREEN/RED press during the greeting leaves 'Y'/'N' pending; the next story session then skips the rotation bookkeeping at :1841 (browse_pending()) and would act on a browse at :1945.

verdicts.reason: Real and reproduced. appsettings.json ContentSync:Stories has 26 rows: 20 real (10 base then 10 alt, all SizeBytes>0) plus 6 Tsivik placeholders that ContentManifestService drops (SizeBytes<=0), so 20 items are offered. cs_manifest_parse caps by POSITION on the offered count (content_sync_model.cpp:36-44 `cap = min(cs_accepted_count(offered), max_out)`), host probe: cs_accepted_count(20)=16, truncated=4, cs_accepted_count(26)=16. Dropped: sutasan-alt, sutlik-orskan-alt, three-piglets-alt, ulik-alt. cs_index_parse also `if (count >= max_out) break;` (content_sync_model.cpp:236), and story_select's s_raw is the same size, so a factory card written with 20 index entries is read as 16 on first boot and rewritten as 16 by the first sync (4 files stranded on the card; orphan sweep is off). Current user-visible effect is nil because alt files are never played (AREG_VARIANT_ENDINGS_ENABLED defaults 0, story_select.cpp:339), so it is latent for the alts. It is NOT latent for anything else: ContentItemOverlay.cs:223 builds `configStories.Concat(uploadedStories)`, so every operator-uploaded story is appended after the 20 config rows and can never pass the 16 cap, and the 6 Tsivik episodes will be cut the same way. This is the same silent-truncation class that was already fixed once for 8 -> 16 (content_sync_rules.h:36-40).
verdicts.reproduced_path: ContentManifestService.cs:48-95 (drops SizeBytes<=0, keeps config order, alt after base) -> device: content_sync.cpp:1744 cs_manifest_parse(..., CS_MAX_STORIES) examines only the first 16 -> :1784/:1802 s_active/carry-forward bounded by CS_MAX_STORIES -> write_index publishes 16. Log line `[content-sync] manifest truncated: 20 offered, max 16, 4 ignored` would show on the bench.

verdicts.test_to_add: RAM math: sizeof(CsStory)=1216 on the x86-64 host (about 1.2 KB on Xtensa), five CsStory[CS_MAX_STORIES] tables (content_sync.cpp:89-91, story_select.cpp:132, AregVoiceMvp.ino:832) = about 6.0 KB per slot: 20 -> +24 KB, 24 -> +49 KB, 32 -> +97 KB (the TLS handshake wants 40-50 KB contiguous internal heap, so 20 is the only size to consider without moving to PSRAM). verdicts.reason: Logic path traced, but fully compiled out today (AREG_VARIANT_ENDINGS_ENABLED defaults 0, story_select.cpp:339-342 `if (0 && ...)`), so no shipped behaviour is wrong; it must be fixed before the flag is turned on. story_heard_mark is called exactly once, at playback START (AregVoiceMvp.ino:1841-1850, gated by `started`), yet the resume comment (:1673-1678) and story_select.h:299-302 both say the heard set is only written at a story's natural END, and rely on that for 'a resume always lands on the same FILE'. With the flag on, parent toggle on and an alt cached: first listen of X plays the base file, X is marked heard at start, pause at byte N (Q&A barge-in, shout pause or sticky pause), resume re-runs story_select_resolve_playback_path(X) (:1673) where story_heard_contains(X) is now true, so it returns X-alt and byte N is applied to a different, separately rendered MP3 (the alts were fully re-rendered, not byte-spliced). The same flip also gives a first listen the alt ending, contradicting 'a FIRST listen always gets the authored ending'.

verdicts.reason: Traced end to end. Turn 12 is allowed to run (online_session_turn_cap_reached(12,12) is false, pinned by host test line 28); after its reply plays the loop unconditionally opens the listen window (LED red via led_for_state(ST_RECORDING), :1160-1180), records the child's answer and builds a WAV (:1193-1214); the for-increment then makes turn_no 13, the loop condition ends the loop, and `if (payload != nullptr) heap_caps_free(payload)` (:1216) discards the recording with no upload and no word. The function's own header says every ending is honest, no lying about what happened; a red 'I am listening' light followed by silent discard breaks that for a 4-7 year old. Cost-wise nothing leaks (no upload), and reaching 12 turns is rare, so it is an honesty/UX flaw, not a safety one.

verdicts.reason: All clip downloads (story clips, welcome/voice, music, game) go through download_file_verified, whose every failure calls story_fail (content_sync.cpp:886-1030), and story_fail sets s_last_status='partial' (:261-265) -- the author's intent is explicit in its comment. The sync_voice/sync_music/sync_games/sync_story_clips `failed` counters are function-local and never returned, and the final verdict (:1932-1949) tests only the narration counter: with failed==0 and index_written it calls set_status("ok","") (:1946), overwriting the 'partial'. content_sync_tick then sees clean (:2133), zeroes s_fail_streak and schedules kCleanRetryMs (6 h) instead of backoff_ms(streak) (5 min). Even the explicit set_status("partial","games_alloc_failed") at :1495 is overwritten the same way. This is not hypothetical: the 2026-08-07 field failure was 78 of 92 game clips failing (`already=14 downloaded=0 failed=78`), which under this verdict reports 'ok' and waits 6 h. The heartbeat then says contentSyncStatus=ok while clips are missing, masking a persistent bad clip. Secondary claim (early returns at :1738/:1753 do not reset s_last_status) is real but minor: it only means an empty/invalid manifest keeps the previous status ('never' on a first attempt counts as not clean, 5 min backoff); accept.
verdicts.reproduced_path: content_sync.cpp:1788 sync_story_clips / :1163 sync_music / :1267 sync_voice / :1406 sync_games -> download_file_verified -> story_fail (partial) -> back in content_sync_run :1932 `failed > 0` false -> :1946 set_status("ok") -> :2133 clean=true -> :2140 delay = kCleanRetryMs.
verdicts.minimal_fix: Add file-scope `int s_item_failures = 0;`; `s_item_failures = 0;` at the top of content_sync_run (next to the other resets, :1639); `s_item_failures++;` in story_fail and in the games_alloc_failed branch (:1495); change the verdict condition at :1932 to `if (failed > 0 || s_item_failures > 0)` and print s_item_failures in the PARTIAL line. Do NOT fix by merely skipping the ok overwrite when status is 'partial': s_last_status is never reset at entry, so a stale 'partial' would stick forever. Side effect to accept knowingly: a permanently bad clip now yields 'partial' with the normal 5/15/60/240 min backoff and can surface the parent-visible E-401 fault for that toy, the same as a bad story does today; the shipped rows are pinned by backend tests so none is expected.

verdicts.reason: The code path exists exactly as described and it breaks the invariant the comment at :655-659 claims ('at no instant are both the primary and the backup absent'): write_index unconditionally runs `if (SD.exists(kIndexBakPath)) SD.remove(kIndexBakPath);` (:674-676) before checking whether the primary exists. If write N's final rename (tmp -> primary, :684) fails, the primary stays absent with the old index only in .bak; write N+1 in the same attempt (there are four writes per sync) deletes that .bak, skips the move because the primary is absent, and if its own rename also fails the tmp is removed too and nothing is left. It needs two rename failures in one attempt after two successful write+read-back verifications, i.e. a card failing in a correlated way, and the consequence is documented as 'wasteful, not corrupting' (content_sync_rules.h:866-868): next boot finds no index and re-downloads everything (~117 MB); no MP3 is touched. Low probability, low impact, in a hardened power-loss path that cannot be compiled or fault-injected here.
verdicts.reproduced_path: content_sync.cpp:684-687 rename(tmp, primary) fails -> returns false, primary absent, .bak good -> next write_index call :674 removes .bak -> :677 `SD.exists(kIndexPath)` false so no move -> :684 rename fails again -> :685 SD.remove(tmp) -> no index files.
verdicts.minimal_fix: For the day someone next edits write_index: `if (SD.exists(kIndexPath)) { if (SD.exists(kIndexBakPath)) SD.remove(kIndexBakPath); if (!SD.rename(kIndexPath, kIndexBakPath)) { ...existing failure branch... } }` then the existing `if (!SD.rename(kIndexTmpPath, kIndexPath))`. When the primary is already missing the .bak is left untouched.

Priority order for the owner: F1 (reboot on a button press, hits the first thing every menu plays and the bedtime music) > F6 > F5 > F3 > F2 (decide before the next story upload or the Tsivik promotion, since uploads are appended after the 20 config rows and are always cut) > F4 (before enabling AREG_VARIANT_ENDINGS_ENABLED) > F7.
